name: towers
description: A tower builds itself from the ground up in four and a half seconds: a Japanese tenshu, a Chinese pagoda or a Thai prang, in one self-contained HTML file.

paragraphs: A tower builds itself from the ground up in four and a half seconds. A cut plane rises through the model and everything below it is finished work — stone, timber, plaster, tile — while the scaffolding waits above the line. Switch the style and the same construction runs as a Japanese tenshu, a Chinese pagoda, a Vietnamese tháp, a Thai prang, a Khmer prasat, or an Ottoman mosque.
features: Six towers modelled at the same level of detail: a Japanese tenshu with stone ishigaki base, plastered storeys and flying eaves; a Chinese pagoda in vermilion lacquer and green glaze under a gilt finial; a Vietnamese…

A construction that runs in 4.40 seconds, captioned by stage in the local language and in English — 石垣普請 / STONEWORK, ថ្មភក់ / SANDSTONE, KUBBE / DOME, MÁI NGÓI / TILED EAVES — with a completion percentage set large in…
Drag to orbit the tower, or just move the pointer and the camera leans with it. The wheel zooms from 50% to 200%. Double-click or press C to recentre.
Scrub the timeline at the foot of the page to sit anywhere in the build, or press Space to pause it mid-air.
Four times of day that cross-fade rather than cut — morning, noon, sunset, night — each with its own sun, fog, ground and sky. Night brings out 39,200 stars.
